001package com.streamConverter.command.impl;
002
003import com.streamConverter.command.AbstractStreamCommand;
004import com.streamConverter.command.rule.IRule;
005import com.streamConverter.command.rule.PassThroughRule;
006import java.io.BufferedReader;
007import java.io.IOException;
008import java.io.InputStream;
009import java.io.InputStreamReader;
010import java.io.OutputStream;
011import java.io.OutputStreamWriter;
012import java.io.Writer;
013import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
014
015/**
016 * CSV Navigate Command Class
017 *
018 * <p>This class implements command for targeted CSV transformation using column selectors. It
019 * identifies specific columns using column names or indices and applies IRule transformations to
020 * those columns while preserving the overall CSV structure.
021 */
022public class CsvNavigateCommand extends AbstractStreamCommand {
023
024  private final String columnSelector;
025  private final IRule rule;
026  private int columnIndex = -1;
027
028  /**
029   * Constructor for CSV navigation with column selector and transformation rule.
030   *
031   * @param columnSelector the column name or index to select (e.g., "name", "2")
032   * @param rule the transformation rule to apply to selected column
033   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if rule is null
034   */
035  public CsvNavigateCommand(String columnSelector, IRule rule) {
036    if (rule == null) {
037      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Rule cannot be null");
038    }
039    this.columnSelector = columnSelector;
040    this.rule = rule;
041  }
042
043  /**
044   * Constructor for CSV navigation with column selector using PassThroughRule.
045   *
046   * @param columnSelector the column name or index to select (e.g., "name", "2")
047   * @deprecated This constructor uses PassThroughRule by default, which may not be the intended
048   *     behavior. Use {@link #CsvNavigateCommand(String, IRule)} to explicitly specify the
049   *     transformation rule. For data extraction without transformation, use {@link
050   *     #extractOnly(String)}.
051   */
052  @Deprecated(since = "1.2.0", forRemoval = true)
053  public CsvNavigateCommand(String columnSelector) {
054    this(columnSelector, new PassThroughRule());
055  }
056
057  /**
058   * Default constructor - processes all columns with PassThroughRule.
059   *
060   * @deprecated This constructor uses PassThroughRule by default, which may not be the intended
061   *     behavior. Use {@link #CsvNavigateCommand(String, IRule)} to explicitly specify the
062   *     transformation rule. For data extraction without transformation, use {@link
063   *     #extractOnly(String)}.
064   */
065  @Deprecated(since = "1.2.0", forRemoval = true)
066  public CsvNavigateCommand() {
067    this(null, new PassThroughRule());
068  }
069
070  /**
071   * Factory method for creating a CSV navigation command that extracts data without transformation.
072   * This method makes the intention explicit: extract data from the specified column as-is.
073   *
074   * @param columnSelector the column name or index to select (e.g., "name", "2")
075   * @return a CsvNavigateCommand that extracts the specified column without transformation
076   */
077  public static CsvNavigateCommand extractOnly(String columnSelector) {
078    return new CsvNavigateCommand(columnSelector, new PassThroughRule());
079  }
080
081  /**
082   * Factory method for creating a CSV navigation command that processes all columns without
083   * transformation. This method makes the intention explicit: process all CSV data as-is.
084   *
085   * @return a CsvNavigateCommand that processes all columns without transformation
086   */
087  public static CsvNavigateCommand extractAll() {
088    return new CsvNavigateCommand(null, new PassThroughRule());
089  }
090
091  @Override
092  protected String getCommandDetails() {
093    String selectorInfo =
094        columnSelector != null
095            ? String.format("columnSelector='%s'", columnSelector)
096            : "all columns";
097    return String.format(
098        "CsvNavigateCommand(%s, rule='%s')", selectorInfo, rule.getClass().getSimpleName());
099  }
100
101  @Override
102  protected void executeInternal(InputStream inputStream, OutputStream outputStream)
103      throws IOException {
104    try (BufferedReader reader =
105            new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(inputStream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
106        Writer writer = new OutputStreamWriter(outputStream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
107
108      if (columnSelector == null) {
109        // Apply rule to entire CSV content
110        applyRuleToEntireCsv(reader, writer);
111      } else {
112        // Apply rule to specific column while preserving structure
113        applyRuleToColumn(reader, writer);
114      }
115    }
116  }
117
118  /** Apply transformation rule to entire CSV content using streaming approach */
119  private void applyRuleToEntireCsv(BufferedReader reader, Writer writer) throws IOException {
120    String line;
121    boolean isFirstLine = true;
122
123    // Stream through CSV lines and apply rule to each line
124    while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
125      if (!isFirstLine) {
126        writer.write(System.lineSeparator());
127      }
128
129      // Apply rule to each line individually to avoid loading entire CSV
130      String transformedLine = rule.apply(line);
131      writer.write(transformedLine);
132
133      isFirstLine = false;
134    }
135
136    writer.flush();
137  }
138
139  /** Apply transformation rule to specific column while preserving CSV structure */
140  private void applyRuleToColumn(BufferedReader reader, Writer writer) throws IOException {
141    String headerLine = reader.readLine();
142    if (headerLine == null) {
143      return; // Empty input
144    }
145
146    String[] headers = parseCSVLine(headerLine);
147
148    // Determine column index if selector is provided
149    columnIndex = findColumnIndex(headers, columnSelector);
150    if (columnIndex == -1) {
151      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Column not found: " + columnSelector);
152    }
153
154    // Write header (unchanged)
155    writer.write(headerLine);
156    writer.write(System.lineSeparator());
157
158    // Process data rows
159    String line;
160    while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
161      String[] values = parseCSVLine(line);
162
163      if (columnIndex < values.length) {
164        // Apply rule to target column only
165        values[columnIndex] = rule.apply(values[columnIndex]);
166      }
167
168      // Write entire row with transformed column (with proper CSV escaping)
169      writer.write(formatCsvRow(values));
170      writer.write(System.lineSeparator());
171    }
172    writer.flush();
173  }
174
175  private String[] parseCSVLine(String line) {
176    return line.split(",(?=([^\"]*\"[^\"]*\")*[^\"]*$)");
177  }
178
179  /** Format CSV row with proper escaping */
180  private String formatCsvRow(String[] values) {
181    StringBuilder row = new StringBuilder();
182    for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
183      if (i > 0) {
184        row.append(",");
185      }
186      row.append(escapeCsvValue(values[i]));
187    }
188    return row.toString();
189  }
190
191  /** Escape CSV value according to CSV standards */
192  private String escapeCsvValue(String value) {
193    if (value == null) {
194      return "";
195    }
196
197    // Check if value needs escaping (contains comma, quote, or newline)
198    if (value.contains(",")
199        || value.contains("\"")
200        || value.contains("\n")
201        || value.contains("\r")) {
202      // Escape quotes by doubling them and wrap entire value in quotes
203      return "\"" + value.replace("\"", "\"\"") + "\"";
204    }
205
206    return value;
207  }
208
209  private int findColumnIndex(String[] headers, String selector) {
210    // Try to find by column name
211    for (int i = 0; i < headers.length; i++) {
212      if (headers[i].trim().equalsIgnoreCase(selector.trim())) {
213        return i;
214      }
215    }
216
217    // Try to parse as column index
218    try {
219      int index = Integer.parseInt(selector);
220      if (index >= 0 && index < headers.length) {
221        return index;
222      }
223    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
224      // Not a number, ignore
225    }
226
227    return -1;
228  }
229}
